title: Can escalation channels redirect reward hacking toward defect disclosure?
abstract: arXiv:2608.29460v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: When coding agents encounter defective test infrastructure they may reward-hack: hardcoding outputs or editing test files to pass tests they cannot legitimately satisfy, a pattern that has now appeared outside benchmarks, in a coordinated multi-agent intrusion of a major AI platform's production infrastructure. The same capability that lets an agent detect and exploit a defect could let it report one, given the right decision environment. We evaluate escalation channels, structured reporting tools available to the agent at the point of conflict, as a decision-environment intervention that both reduces reward hacking and surfaces the infrastructure defects that trigger it. A $2 \times 2$ factorial separates the contributions of an escalation tool, a standalone anti-reward-hacking policy, and their combination. translated_title: 上报渠道能否将奖励黑客行为转向缺陷披露？
translated_abstract: 当代码智能体遇到有缺陷的测试基础设施时，可能会进行奖励黑客行为：硬编码输出或编辑测试文件，以通过它们无法合法满足的测试。这种模式如今已出现在基准测试之外，出现在对某大型AI平台生产基础设施的协调式多智能体入侵事件中。让智能体能够检测并利用缺陷的同一能力，在合适的决策环境下，也可以让它转而上报缺陷。我们评估了上报渠道——即在冲突发生时可供智能体使用的结构化报告工具——作为一种决策环境干预手段，它既能减少奖励黑客行为，又能暴露出触发该行为的底层基础设施缺陷。一项2×2因子实验设计分离了上报工具、独立的反奖励黑客策略以及二者组合各自的贡献。在涵盖5个模型家族的8个前沿模型上，组合干预将奖励黑客行为从23.6%降低到5.3%（混合效应模型……）
tldr: 该论文提出在代码智能体遭遇测试基础设施缺陷时为其提供结构化上报工具（上报渠道），可将其奖励黑客行为从23.6%降至5.3%，同时暴露出触发该行为的底层缺陷。
en_tdlr: Escalation channels—structured reporting tools available to coding agents at the point of conflict—reduce reward hacking from 23.6% to 5.3% across 8 frontier models while surfacing the underlying infrastructure defects that trigger it.
